title: Efficient Classical Simulation of Weakly Interacting Fermion Dynamics
authors: Chu Zhao, Iman Marvian, Yu Tong
abstract: We consider the task of simulating the real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems. In particular, we focus on computing the expectation value of a local observable $A$ at time $t$. By analyzing the convergence of the perturbative expansion in the interaction strength $λ$ for the Heisenberg-picture observable, we propose a polynomial-time algorithm for estimating this expectation value in the weakly interacting regime $λ|t|^{2D+1}=\mathcal{O}(1)$, when the Hamiltonian is geometrically local on a $D$-dimensional lattice. Importantly, this condition is independent of the system size. If the goal is instead to approximate the time-evolved observable in normalized Frobenius norm, we extend the convergence regime to $λ|t|=\mathcal{O}(1)$ with quasi-polynomial runtime. When the non-interacting part exhibits Anderson localization, our polynomial-time algorithm can be extended up to $λ|t|=\mathcal{O}(1)$, modulo polylogarithmic factors. Our algorithm brings together ideas from continuous-time QMC, diagrammatic QMC, and Majorana Propagation, but with a new Heisenberg-picture operator-growth analysis that makes the sampling complexity rigorously controllable. This leads to provably efficient classical algorithms in regimes where the interaction is weak enough that the sampling variance remains bounded independently of system size. Together, these results identify broad regimes in which weak interactions, locality, and localization can be leveraged to make real-time fermionic dynamics classically tractable.
summary: This work develops provably efficient classical algorithms to simulate the real-time evolution of weakly interacting fermionic systems. By analyzing the perturbative expansion in the interaction strength, the authors establish specific parameter regimes where the simulation remains classically tractable. This advances the field by providing rigorous complexity bounds for dynamics in weakly perturbed, local quantum many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently simulating the real-time dynamics of weakly interacting fermionic systems by computing the expectation value of a local observable.
main_result: It proposes a polynomial-time algorithm for estimating this expectation value in the weakly interacting regime, with extensions to quasi-polynomial time and regimes exhibiting Anderson localization.
method: The core method involves analyzing the perturbative expansion (Dyson series) of the time evolution operator in the Heisenberg picture, utilizing a randomized sampling algorithm controlled by the Majorana 1-norm.
model_or_system: The system is a weakly interacting fermionic system on a D-dimensional lattice, governed by a Hamiltonian $H = H_0 + \lambda V$, where $H_0$ is the non-interacting part and $\lambda V$ is the weak interaction perturbation.
key_observables: The expectation value of a local observable $A$ at time $t$, i.e., $	ext{Tr}(ho_0 e^{iHt} A e^{-iHt})$.
important_parameters: The critical parameters are the interaction strength $\lambda$ and time $t$, defining regimes like $\lambda|t|^{2D+1}=\mathcal{O}(1)$ for polynomial time.
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian must be geometrically local on a D-dimensional lattice, and the analysis relies on controlling the error using the Majorana 1-norm.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem, derives the perturbative expansion, introduces the randomized sampling algorithm based on the Majorana 1-norm, and presents theorems defining the convergence regimes and computational complexity.
why_interesting: The rigorous control over sampling variance and the explicit derivation of polynomial-time algorithms for real-time dynamics in weakly interacting systems provide powerful, general tools for studying non-equilibrium quantum phenomena.
